Event.Description: Account failed to log on. Logon Type: 3 (Network). Failure Reason: Unknown username or bad password. Source IP: 203.0.113.42 (external). Failure count: 47 attempts in 5 minutes. Possible brute force attack against the e-training portal admin account.

Account failed to log on. Logon Type: 3 (Network). Failure Reason: Unknown username or bad password. Source IP: 203.0.113.42 (external). Same external IP targeting default administrator account after admin account lockout triggered.

Special privileges assigned to new logon. User jdoe was granted SeDebugPrivilege and SeTcbPrivilege — privileges typically reserved for SYSTEM-level processes. This account is a standard trainee account with no administrative role. Possible token impersonation or local privilege escalation exploit.

New process created: cmd.exe spawned by w3wp.exe (IIS worker process). Command line: cmd.exe /c whoami && net user && ipconfig /all. A web process spawning a command shell is a strong indicator of webshell execution or remote code injection. Investigate immediately.

User account admin was locked out on domain controller DC01. Caller computer name: 192.168.1.10. The account was locked after exceeding the maximum failed logon threshold (5 attempts). Triggered by the brute force activity observed at 08:14.

A logon was attempted using explicit credentials. User jdoe used net use to map a drive to \\192.168.1.5\ADMIN$ (domain controller admin share) using alternate credentials. This lateral movement attempt indicates the attacker may have obtained domain credentials.

A scheduled task was created. Task Name: \Microsoft\Windows\UpdateCheck. Action: powershell.exe -enc [base64 encoded payload]. This task is not part of any authorized software deployment. Base64-encoded PowerShell in a scheduled task is a common persistence and C2 beacon technique.

Attempt to access object. Object: C:\Users\All Users\Application Data\Microsoft\Windows\WER\. Access: ReadData. User msmith does not have authorized access to this directory. Multiple access attempts to sensitive system directories detected within a 10-minute window.

Firewall policy violation detected. Outbound connection blocked from 192.168.1.20 to 45.33.32.156:4444 (known Metasploit default port). Traffic matched threat intel feed for command-and-control (C2) communication. Connection originated from IIS worker process on the API gateway server.

The audit log was cleared. Subject Account Name: jdoe. This event indicates an attempt to cover attack tracks by wiping the Security event log on the compromised API gateway server. Log clearing following privilege escalation and lateral movement is a strong indicator of an active intrusion.
